entries.name: USP10 deubiquitinates monoUb:K164,ISG:K164,ISG:K168-PCNA
entries.summation: USP10 acts as a ubiquitin protease to remove ubiquitin from lysine K164 residue of doubly ISGylated PCNA. Deubiquitination of PCNA by USP10 causes dissociation of Y family DNA damage bypass polymerases, thus ending translesion DNA synthesis (TLS) and limiting TLS-induced mutagenesis (Park et al. 2014).

entries.name: USP10 binds monoUb:K164,ISG:K164,ISG:K168-PCNA
entries.summation: Ubiquitin protease USP10 binds doubly ISGylated and monoubiquitinated PCNA (Park et al. 2014). PCNA exists as a homotrimer so that the ISGylation and monoubiquitination occur on different subunits.
